thread:
alyssa: apiserver in eu-west1 is flapping since the GPU scale-in at ~01:03 UTC. getting spikes of 5xx and controller-manager restarts. anyone seeing this?

raj: on it. initial glance: lots of pod evictions from the new descheduler job right before the spike. could be eviction fanout causing watch/etcd pressure.

sre-bot: incident detected - apiserver_error_rate > 4% for 120s in eu-west1. severity: high. alerts: #pagerduty.

marta: confirmed. etcd leader stepped down ~01:03:27, write latency spiked to 250-400ms for ~90s. controller-manager leader election churned twice. kube-apiserver logs show many 429/503 for list/watch.

raj: paste of recent logs: ```
E0308 01:03:27.123456 1 reflector.go:205] pkg/mod/k8s.io/client-go/...: watch of *v1.Pod ended: too old resource version: 123456 (429)
E0308 01:03:28.987654 1 server.go:789] apiserver: unable to respond: etcdserver: request timed out
```

john: also saw a surge in events from the scheduler when those pods were being evicted -> event fanout. kube-apiserver memory stayed ok but CPU jittered.

devops-oncall: I just rolled back descheduler helm release in eu-west1 from v2.1.4 -> v2.1.3 and paused the job for the GPU nodepool. will monitor. :thumbsup:

alyssa: good call. is this a descheduler bug or sizing/ordering issue when many GPU nodes scale in quickly?

marta: a mix. descheduler eviction created thousands of deletes + evictions in a short window. our apiserver replicas are 3 for control plane; with leader stepdown + etcd write latency that was enough to trip the error budget.

raj: mitigation checklist I'm running through: 1) pause descheduler 2) increase apiserver replicas to 5 in eu-west1 (temp) 3) bump controller-manager lease duration to 15s and renewDeadline to 10s 4) enable event aggregation plugin to reduce fanout. doing 1 & 2 now.

devops-oncall: running: `kubectl -n kube-system scale deploy/kube-apiserver --replicas=5 --context=eu-west1-control` (rolling, watch logs)

john: also suggest we add a descheduler guard: if nodepool is scaling-in, avoid mass evictions. we have a node-annotation for scale-events; descheduler should respect it.

marta: agreed. long-term: add cordon+drain rate limit for GPU pools and prefer graceful eviction over immediate. that'll reduce event storm and etcd churn.

alyssa: cost tradeoff note: increasing apiserver replicas temporarily increases control plane cost but stabilizes production revenue traffic. for recurring prevention we should tune descheduler + nodepool lifecycle rather than permanent replicas.

raj: adding a short-term autoscript to disable descheduler during scheduled nodepool updates. will PR tomorrow.

devops-oncall: noticing API errors decreasing after rollback and scale to 5. error rate down to 0.8% in last 60s.

sre-bot: incident status: mitigated. watch until 02:00 UTC.

alyssa: next steps captured: - patch descheduler to respect nodepool-scaling annotation (owner: infra) - add rate-limit to drain operations for GPU pools (owner: eng-runtime) - update runbook: include descheduler rollback step and apiserver scale play (owner: eng-sre) - follow-up postmortem if recurrence.

john: pinging infra to add a cheaper reserved cushion for GPU pools in eu-west1 so we don't autoscale so aggressively and trigger flash-scale-ins. cost vs reliability tradeoff for product team.

raj: logging the incident in incidents/ with IDs and timeline. will include graphs: etcd commit latency, apiserver 5xx, descheduler eviction rate, nodepool scale events.

marta: FYI for postmortem - include etcd metrics: raft leader changes, proposal durations, compaction events. those helped confirm write latency was the root amplification.

alyssa: thanks all. keep monitoring and post the postmortem link once ready. :face_with_head_bandage:
